text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz sent back the Conflict of Interest Act to Parliament yesterday, as he disagreed with some of its provisions. @

- The Wall Street Journal Europe wrote on Thursday that Prime Minister Gyula Horn significantly improved Hungary's chances of joining NATO when he signed the basic treaty with Romania. Meanwhile, the New York Times quoted US and NATO experts as saying the biggest obstacle to admission is the communist-era mentality.

- According to preliminary figure, the budget closed the year with a deficit of HUF 153 billion, while the public finance deficit was 3.7 percent of GDP, 0.3 percent below the target set in an agreement with the IMF. @

- Smallholder President Jozsef Torgyan announced Thursday that 42-year-old attorney Attila Bank of Debrecen, the party's deputy general secretary, will take up the parliamentary seat of Miklos K. Csontos, who was killed last Friday.
- The average yield of three-month discount T-bills dropped to 22.08 percent from 22.24 in Thursday's auction after rising in the three preceding auctions. @

- Matav is expected to award the leadership of its international share offering to the US company Merrill Lynch, a report refers to a story in Thursday's Financial Times. Matav seeks to become the first Central European company to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
- The Finance Ministry repurchased Polgari Bank from Budapest Bank for HUF 1.1 billion on December 23, ministry officials revealed at a press conference yesterday.
- The board of directors at CIB Rt. have elected former National Bank vice president Frigyes Harshegyi director of capital market operations, effective February 1. @
- An unidentified man killed a co-owner of agricultural wholesaler Mezoker Kft. at a company warehouse in Bekescsaba on Wednesday in an apparent murder-robbery.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Parliament will debate 61 bills and amendment, one-third of them dealing with economic matters, according to the preliminary legislative programme.
- The Securities and Exchange Commission has extended its ban on trading by Vektor Broker Rt. to January 31. @

- Geza Jakab, head of the Budapest Police's investigative division, said police have suspects in the recent series of explosions and attacks, but do not have enough information to initiate criminal proceedings.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs departs for Israel on Sunday.
VILAGGAZDASAG @

- British Trade Secretary Ian Lang will visit Hungary in the near future as part of a UK government campaign to encourage British trade and capital investment in Hungary, the Czech Republic, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.
- A total of $1.5 billion in foreign capital flowed into Hungary in the first ten months of last year, according to a preliminary study by the Ministry of Industry.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The chemical company Nitrokemia Rt. had sales of HUF 13.5 billion last year, the same as the previous year. @
- The dairy company Zalatej Rt. achieved net sales of HUF 13.8 billion, but made no profit last year.
